### Step 1: Setup: collect and shuffle

Imports, then glob the stimuli and shuffle them. Print the list: twelve paths, different order each run. *(Careful with the shuffle gotcha: [Chapter 7](07_random.qmd).)*

:::: {.content-visible when-meta="show-solutions-s2"}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show the code"}
```python
from psychopy import visual, event, core
import glob
import random

images = glob.glob('stimuli/stimulus*.jpg')
random.shuffle(images)
print(images)
```

### Step 3: Welcome and instructions

The participant has never seen this task: the welcome text must teach the rule. Lion → press the *opposite* arrow; burrow → press *its* side. Wait for any key.

:::: {.content-visible when-meta="show-solutions-s2"}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show the code"}
```python
welcome = visual.TextStim(win, color='white', height=0.06,
    text='The Fleeing Rabbit\n\n'
         'You are the rabbit - and the lion is on the hunt!\n\n'
         'See a LION?  Run the other way: press the OPPOSITE arrow.\n'
         'See a BURROW?  Dive in: press the arrow on ITS side.\n\n'
         'Be quick - and be right. Press any key to start.')
welcome.draw()
win.flip()
event.waitKeys()
```

When it all runs: switch `fullscr=True`, run it once *as a participant*, and notice whether the lion trials feel harder than the burrow trials. Hold that thought for [Chapter 11](11_cogcomm.qmd).

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Checkpoint · complete Fleeing Rabbit script"}
```python
from psychopy import visual, event, core
import glob
import random

# --- setup ---
images = glob.glob('stimuli/stimulus*.jpg')
random.shuffle(images)

win = visual.Window(size=(1280, 720), fullscr=False,
                    color='black', checkTiming=False)

# --- welcome screen ---
welcome = visual.TextStim(win, color='white', height=0.06,
    text='The Fleeing Rabbit\n\n'
         'You are the rabbit - and the lion is on the hunt!\n\n'
         'See a LION?  Run the other way: press the OPPOSITE arrow.\n'
         'See a BURROW?  Dive in: press the arrow on ITS side.\n\n'
         'Be quick - and be right. Press any key to start.')
welcome.draw()
win.flip()
event.waitKeys()

# --- trial loop ---
for image in images:
    # show the stimulus
    stim = visual.ImageStim(win, image=image)
    stim.draw()
    win.flip()

    # collect the response
    keys = event.waitKeys(keyList=['left', 'right'])
    key = keys[0]

    # derive the correct answer from the filename
    if image.endswith('_L.jpg'):
        correct_key = 'left'
    else:
        correct_key = 'right'

    # conditional feedback, shown for 2 seconds
    if key == correct_key:
        feedback = visual.ImageStim(win, image='stimuli/success.jpg')
    else:
        feedback = visual.ImageStim(win, image='stimuli/failure.jpg')

    feedback.draw()
    win.flip()
    core.wait(2)

# --- goodbye and shutdown ---
goodbye = visual.TextStim(win, text='That was it - thank you!', color='white')
goodbye.draw()
win.flip()
core.wait(2)

win.close()
core.quit()
```

**Keep this script safe.** Session 3 extends it: clock, logfile, and your Portfolio 2 prototype.
:::

```python
# before the loop:
n_correct = 0

# in the correct-answer branch:
n_correct = n_correct + 1

# goodbye message:
goodbye = visual.TextStim(win,
    text=f'The rabbit escaped {n_correct} of {len(images)} times. Thank you!',
    color='white')
```

**C. Write a reusable function.** The prepare-draw-flip-wait pattern repeats constantly: exactly what functions are for. We never got to functions live in Session 1, but the [chapter is online](../session1-python/09_functions.qmd); this is the perfect excuse.

:::: {.content-visible when-meta="show-solutions-s2"}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show the code"}
```python
def show_image(win, image_path, keyList=None):
    stim = visual.ImageStim(win, image=image_path)
    stim.draw()
    win.flip()
    keys = event.waitKeys(keyList=keyList)
    return keys[0]

# the trial loop becomes wonderfully short:
for image in images:
    key = show_image(win, image, keyList=['left', 'right'])
    ...
```
